notes: Both candidates fail the crux identically — they attribute the MESH_NODE_HEALTH reportedAt heartbeat to the killed agent process, when mesh-health-publisher (a separate service) writes it, so both predicted fed.* watcher transitions are false. B is otherwise far more accurate and runnable: its circling-side chain (snapshot guard, dead-marking, isCirclingStepComplete barrier, advance-not-abort, no-explicit-degrade-status) matches mesh-task-daemon.js and mesh-collab.js almost line-for-line, its constants (90s threshold, 120s TTL, BROKEN detail string, services[].pid) all check out, and two of its defect alternates map to regressions literally documented in the cited sources. A piles on independent errors — a false BROKEN-to-WORKING recovery claim, an abort path via sweepCollabRoundTimeouts which explicitly skips circling_strategy mode, an invented stale_members field, and RELEASED/markFailed conflation — with only the 60s sweep cadence and a genuinely OFF-restoring cleanup as offsetting strengths.
